subject: English
q: Who is C. V. Raman, and what is he famous for?
ans: C. V. Raman was a great Indian scientist. He is famous for discovering the Raman Effect.

subject: English
q: C. V. Raman showed great interest in science from his early days. Justify.
ans: Even as a boy, Raman made a model of a dynamo. During his school days he borrowed science books from college students and read them. He excelled in Mathematics and Physics from an early age.

subject: English
q: Why couldn't Raman go to the United Kingdom for higher studies?
ans: After his M.A., Raman wanted to go to the United Kingdom for higher studies in science, but his health broke down and he could not go. This was the greatest disappointment of his life.

subject: English
q: How can you say that Raman was a kind man?
ans: When Raman was working as Deputy Accountant General, a villager came to him with some badly burnt hundred-rupee notes. Raman took pity on him and exchanged the burnt notes for new ones.

subject: English
q: What discovery did C. V. Raman make and how did it affect physics?
ans: Raman discovered the Raman Effect, which explains the scattering of light. It had a great impact on the field of physics and helped scientists study light and matter.

subject: English
q: Describe the incident which led to the discovery of the Raman Effect.
ans: Raman was conducting experiments on the scattering of light in liquids by passing light through various materials. His careful observation and analysis of the scattered light led to the discovery of the Raman Effect in 1928.

subject: English
q: Mention the awards received by Sir C. V. Raman.
ans: In 1929 he was knighted by King George V and became Sir C. V. Raman. In 1930 he won the Nobel Prize for Physics. In 1954 the Government of India awarded him the Bharat Ratna. In 1957 the Soviet Union honoured him with the International Lenin Prize.

subject: English
q: Write a short note on Sir C. V. Raman.
ans: C. V. Raman was a famous Indian scientist. He was born on 7 November 1888 in Tiruchirappalli (Trichy), Tamil Nadu. He discovered the Raman Effect in 1928. He received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930 and was the first Indian to win a Nobel Prize in science. He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1954.

b) Savings Bank account
c) 1000 rupees
d) Five hundred rupees

q: Why did the narrator's spirit laugh at him?

subject: English
q: What does the story teach us?
ans: The story teaches us about universal brotherhood and that we should not judge people by their colour.

subject: English
q: "Exercise is good for me," says the narrator. What was the exercise?

subject: English
q: What did the narrator see on his way home the first day?
ans: He saw two little boys playing in a yard – one black and one white. The black boy was giving orders and the white boy was obeying him.

subject: English
q: Why did the narrator feel disturbed after seeing the boys' play?
ans: He was disturbed because he thought it was unusual for a white boy to obey a black boy like a servant, which went against the common social views of that time.

subject: English
q: What change did the narrator observe the next day?
ans: The next day he saw the same boys playing again, but this time the white boy was giving the commands and the black boy was obeying.

subject: English
q: What lesson did the narrator learn from the boys?
ans: He realised that children do not think about race or colour the way adults do, and that his earlier assumptions were wrong.

subject: English
q: Describe the physical appearance of the two boys in the lesson.
ans: One boy was perhaps four years old and the other five. The bigger one was a sturdy youngster, very dark, with a mat of coarse hair and coal-black eyes. The other was white, with hazel eyes and light-brown hair. Both were dressed in blue shirts and khaki pants.

subject: English
q: How does the story show that children don't care about race?
ans: The two boys, one black and one white, play together by switching roles every day. They treat each other as equals, unlike adults who make biased assumptions about colour.

subject: English
q: What was the narrator's thinking before and after seeing the boys the next day?
ans: On the first day, seeing the black boy command the white boy, the narrator thought it showed racial superiority and felt disturbed. On the second day he saw the white boy giving commands and realised it was only a game in which they took turns. This freed him from his racial assumptions.
